findings.body: TopicUser.find_by returns nil and the following `tu.notification_level` / `tu.save!` calls raise NoMethodError, causing a 500 error instead of unsubscribing the user.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime NoMethodError crashes the request when no TopicUser record exists.
findings.impact: TopicUser.find_by returns nil and the following `tu.notification_level` / `tu.save!` calls raise NoMethodError, causing a 500 error instead of unsubscribing the user.
findings.root_cause: New unsubscribe action assumes a TopicUser record always exists for the current user/topic pair without checking for nil.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard against a missing record, e.g. `tu ||= TopicUser.new(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` or return a friendly error/redirect when tu is nil before mutating it.
findings.title: TopicUser lookup in unsubscribe action is not nil-checked before use
findings.trigger: A logged-in user who was notified about a topic (e.g. mentioned or invited to a PM) but never visited/tracked it clicks the unsubscribe link in the email, so no TopicUser row exists for that user/topic pair.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R105 shows `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` which returns nil when no record exists. Lines R107-R113 immediately call `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!` without nil check. A user notified about a topic but who never visited it would have no TopicUser record, causing NoMethodError.

raw_findings.body: Comparing nil with an Integer (`nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`) raises NoMethodError, crashing the unsubscribe request for such users.
raw_findings.failure_mode: NoMethodError: undefined method `>' for nil:NilClass when notification_level is unset.
raw_findings.impact: Comparing nil with an Integer (`nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`) raises NoMethodError, crashing the unsubscribe request for such users.
raw_findings.root_cause: The unsubscribe action does not account for the nullable notification_level column that is treated as 'regular' by convention elsewhere in the model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Default the nil case explicitly, e.g. `level = tu.notification_level || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` before comparing/assigning.
raw_findings.title: notification_level may be nil when compared in unsubscribe action
raw_findings.trigger: A TopicUser record exists for the user/topic but its notification_level column was never explicitly set (nil), which the codebase elsewhere treats as 'regular' via COALESCE (see TopicUser.tracking scope).
